name: Lind’s comparative scurvy treatment
description: Aboard HMS Salisbury, James Lind compared six approaches to scurvy among twelve sailors, observing improvement in the pair given citrus.

date.basis: Date applies to the stated documented event or archaeological context, not to a worldwide origin.

events.statement: Aboard HMS Salisbury, James Lind compared six approaches to scurvy among twelve sailors, observing improvement in the pair given citrus.

evidence.supports: Lind compared six treatments for scurvy among 12 sailors in 1747; the pair given citrus improved. The museum account says the British Admiralty required lemon juice in 1795. This small comparison was not randomized.

events.caveats: Citrus was known before Lind. The comparison involved only two people per treatment and did not use random allocation or blinding; its publication followed in 1753.
